node.title: Customers
node.explanation: People who walk in. More of them means more cups sold.

node.title: Long queue
node.explanation: When the line is too long, some people leave without buying.

node.title: Cups sold
node.subtitle: Per day
node.explanation: How many drinks the shop sells in a day.

node.title: Price per cup
node.explanation: What one drink costs the customer.
Cups sold multiplied by the price per cup.

node.title: Revenue
node.explanation: All the money that comes in from sales.

node.title: Costs
node.explanation: What the shop pays out to keep running.

node.title: Beans and milk
node.explanation: Ingredients. This cost rises with every cup sold.

node.title: Rent and staff
node.explanation: Fixed costs. The shop pays them however many cups it sells.

node.title: Profit
node.explanation: What is left of revenue after all costs are paid.

node.explanation: Each cup sold is one unit of the business: it brings in its price and uses up beans and milk.

edge.label: buy
edge.explanation: Customers buy drinks; each purchase is a cup sold.
A long queue stops some sales: people give up and leave.
Raise the price too far and fewer people come in.
Cups sold go into the sum.
The price goes into the sum.
Cups sold times price gives the result.
Cups sold times price becomes the day's revenue.
More revenue means more profit, if costs stay the same.
Every cost paid comes out of profit.
Every cup needs beans and milk, so this cost grows with sales.

edge.label: one of these
edge.explanation: The drawing shows a single cup, the unit being counted.
